text:
Talia Benson: Kicking off AWS Marketplace listing refresh thread. I got our AWS partner contact confirmed (Rita S., Marketplace Partner PM). She wants: updated listing copy + required fields, screenshots, and the security packet attachments by end of next week so they can hold a review slot.

Talia Benson: Key dates from Rita:
- Draft submission to AWS (all fields populated): Fri Feb 7
- Partner review feedback back to us: ~5–7 biz days
- Target publish week: Feb 24 (assuming no major security claim issues)

Talia Benson: Required AWS listing fields she called out (not exhaustive):
- Product name + short description (<= 200 chars)
- Long description (benefits + how it works)
- Pricing model / dimensions + any usage notes
- Support info (email, support hours, SLA language if any)
- Categories + keywords
- Region availability statement (where service is available)
- EULA / terms link
- Fulfillment: SaaS contract + entitlements mapping notes (they’ll ask how buyer gets provisioned)

Talia Benson: Owners (proposed) — please confirm / adjust:
- Listing copy + keywords: @Soojin Lee
- Screenshots (Console + onboarding flow): @Elliot Price (coord w/ Design + Kira)
- Security packet + evidence index + “allowed to share”: @Olga Petrov + @Marcus Lin (sign-off: Dr. Aisha Rahman)
- Launch readiness checklist / submission logistics: me + @Connor O'Brien

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: I can own copy/keywords. Do we have AWS character limits for the long description + bullets? Also do they want the “Why buy via marketplace” section in the listing itself or as an attachment?

Talia Benson: Rita said long description is flexible but they prefer scannable sections + bullets. They do care about “deployment steps” being explicit (purchase -> link org -> start using). They also want the support contact and refund/cancellation language to be clear.

Camila Reyes: For screenshots, let’s keep it tight. AWS reviewers get picky if UI looks inconsistent. We should pick 3–5 max:
1) Console org-linking step
2) Entitlement status page
3) Usage dashboard (cost/latency) — optional
4) Security/compliance page (only if we can keep wording accurate)

Elliot Price: I can coordinate screenshot inventory. Quick q: are we expected to provide an architecture diagram as well (data flow, where prompts/outputs live, etc.)?

Talia Benson: Yes. Rita asked for at least one diagram explaining SaaS boundaries + data flow (high level). She flagged that it helps with reviewer questions around “where is customer data processed/stored.”

Marcus Lin: On security packet: we need to be very careful with claims in the listing text itself. AWS will reject if we imply “no data stored” without nuance. Also need to align on audit logs / retention statements.

Olga Petrov: +1. Also reminder: SOC 2 report is NDA-only. We can include a “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA” statement + attach the bridge/attestation letter if approved. I’ll confirm what we can share directly to AWS reviewers.

Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll stick to approved phrasing. Can someone drop the latest “do/don’t” language for security/compliance claims? I remember we had a block like “encryption in transit/at rest” + “customer-managed keys supported for Private” but not for every SKU.

Marcus Lin: Use this guardrail:
- OK: “Encryption in transit and at rest” (but specify scope: service data stores + backups)
- OK: “Audit logs available” (but specify what events and where they can be exported)
- NOT OK: “HIPAA compliant” unless we have signed BAA + specific scope
- Be explicit: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private controls differ

Connor O'Brien: From release perspective: if submission is Feb 7, we need final screenshots by Feb 5 latest. Otherwise we’ll slip the package.

Lauren Bishop: For Dedicated SKU language: please route through me before we submit. Buyers will interpret Dedicated as “single-tenant VPC” unless we spell out the isolation model clearly.

Talia Benson: Action items (this week):
- @Soojin Lee: v1 listing copy draft by Tue EOD (headline, short desc, long desc sections, keywords). Include “deployment steps” section.
- @Elliot Price: screenshot + diagram inventory by Wed (owners + where in Console). Flag anything requiring redaction.
- @Olga Petrov / @Marcus Lin: security packet “AWS reviewer” version by Thu (what we can attach + what’s NDA-only).
- @Connor O'Brien: submission checklist + internal review schedule by Wed.

Soojin Lee: Copy draft by Tue works. I’ll include placeholders like [SCREENSHOT-1] so we can map them cleanly.

Elliot Price: Screenshot inventory: I’ll pull Kira in offline for the Console steps + make sure the org-linking UI matches current build. If the onboarding wizard is still behind a flag, we’ll need a staging environment with stable state.

Marcus Lin: Re: staging: please ensure screenshots don’t include real customer org names / IDs. Use a seeded “Acme Marketplaces Test” org.

Olga Petrov: I’m going to add a one-liner in the packet: “Compliance artifacts are provided upon request under NDA.” AWS reviewers usually accept that.

Camila Reyes: Also please make sure the listing copy is consistent with what Sales is saying. The #1 thing buyers ask: “How does marketplace purchase map to our Redwood org and entitlements?” If we can answer that in 3 steps, it will reduce escalations.

Talia Benson: Yup. I’ll draft the 3-step provisioning blurb for AWS:
1) Purchase in AWS Marketplace
2) Click ‘Set up your account’ -> link AWS account to Redwood org
3) Entitlements activate automatically (typical < X mins); status visible in Console
We’ll leave X as “a few minutes” unless Engineering gives a hard SLO.

Elliot Price: :eyes: on the “few minutes” language — we’ve seen entitlement lag. Maybe say “typically within a few minutes; if not active within 30 minutes contact support@…”?

Talia Benson: Good call. I’ll phrase it with the 30-min support threshold.

Soojin Lee: One more: AWS asked for “Support escalation path” — do we want to publish a dedicated alias like marketplace-support@ or just use support@redwoodinference.com?

Connor O'Brien: Prefer support@ for now. Less alias sprawl. We can add a tag in Zendesk later.

Marcus Lin: For security contact, we should provide security@ (we already use that for vuln disclosure / questionnaires). Separate from support.

Talia Benson: Great. I’ll include:
- Support: support@redwoodinference.com
- Security: security@redwoodinference.com

Talia Benson: Next touchpoint: I’ll schedule a 25-min internal review Thu 10:30am PT (Copy + Security packet + screenshot list). Goal is no surprises before Feb 7 submission.

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup:

Olga Petrov: :thumbsup: I’ll come with a clean “AWS attachment list” and what needs NDA.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: I’ll bring screenshot inventory + diagram draft outline.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: Copy draft coming Tue.

Connor O'Brien: Ack. I’ll send calendar + checklist doc link in-channel once ready.
